rooms.long:
White foam churns over a fractured shoreline where the ocean meets the
land. To the north, a desolate beachhead stretches toward the interior of
a silent island. A small, waterlogged boat drifts aimlessly in the surf,
its wood bleached white by years of salt and sun.

Shattered timber from a fallen pier litters the shoreline, half-buried in
shifting sands. To the north, the silent spires of a vacant city loom over
the dunes like jagged teeth against a stagnant twilight. The rotted ribs
of a great yacht emerge from the surf to the east, stripped of all glory.
Only the rhythmic thundering of the western falls breaks the heavy silence.

rooms.short: A narrow path between the dunes
rooms.long:
High, shifting mounds of sand wall in this narrow corridor. To the north,
two salt-pitted stone pillars stand like skeletal sentinels marking a
forgotten threshold. The path leads south toward the sound of the surf
and north toward the looming city silhouette.

Sand gives way to jagged stone as the path climbs toward the city's
outer perimeter. To the north, the monolithic gate towers cast long,
immobile shadows over the shifting ground. The air is thinner here,
carrying only the scent of dry dust and ancient, sun-baked rock.

Two monolithic pillars rise into the stagnant sky, their stone faces
pitted by centuries of salt and wind. Hollow cavities, once serving as
watch-posts, stare like empty eye sockets to the east and west. Faded
runes are carved deep into the rock, though only the word 'Welcome'
remains legible. To the north, a brick-paved street stretches between
rows of cold, metallic torches.

rooms.short: Intersection of Silver Street and Balin Road
rooms.long:
Polished stone meets weathered brick at this silent junction. To the
north, the pale length of Silver Street stretches toward the hollow
shells of distant temples. Four massive metallic torches stand at the
corners, their frames blackened and cold. The bustling crowds are long
gone, leaving only the wind to whistle through the empty thoroughfares.

Smooth, pale stone lines this wide thoroughfare under a stagnant sky.
Dead metallic torches stand in silent intervals, their glow long since
extinguished. To the east, an ornate building rises toward the heavens
with twin, crumbling spires. Opposite the spires, a nameless storefront
stares onto the street with a vacant, open doorway.

The pale stones of the street remain eerily clear of debris, as if the
city itself refuses to decay. To the west, a massive, cold furnace marks
the remains of a foundry. The eastern storefront, once smelling of grain
and yeast, now exhales only the scent of damp flour and rot. Northward,
the shadows of monumental structures loom over the cooling metal torches.

The pale street-stones lead toward a wide, patterned plaza to the north.
Row upon row of glass-domed torches stand like sightless eyes, their
inner fires long since spent. To the east, the sharp, medicinal tang of
evaporated spirits lingers in the air. A low wall to the west overlooks
a choked canal where black, motionless water reflects only the gray sky.

Intricate brickwork spreads across this vast expanse, forming faded
crests and silver crosses that bleed into the surrounding stone. In the
center, a gnarled tree erupts from a raised circular dais, its roots
cracking the masonry in a slow, silent conquest. A forest of metallic
torches stands frozen around the perimeter, their glass housings clouded
by time. To the north, the path climbs toward a high, shadowed hill.

The street-stones here possess a cold, unnatural sheen, untouched by
dust or debris. To the south lies the sprawling emptiness of the grand
plaza. Row upon row of metallic torches line the path, their glass
domes emitting a sharp, static hum that vibrates in the stagnant air.
A pale blue luminescence spills from a storefront to the west, while
to the east, the dark canal laps silently against the street's edge.

The street stretches north and south, caught in a cold, unwavering light.
To the east, the muffled roar of the hidden canal vibrates through the
walls of a derelict shop. A massive, ornate structure dominates the
western view, its smooth facade offering no entry. To the south, the
distant glow of the plaza is a dim, dying amber against the gray horizon.

A sterile, white radiance bathes this section of the street, emanating
from metallic torches that hum with ancient power. To the west, the
imposing facade of a temple-like structure bears a weathered sign: 'The
Hall of Mazarbul'. An iron fence to the east cordons off a vacant, dust-
choked lot. The pale road continues its path north and south, cutting
a clean line through the silent, surrounding ruins.

The pavement here is fractured and charred, leading toward the jagged
base of a mountain to the north. To the east, the walls of a blackened
structure still radiate a dull, rhythmic heat, pulsing like a dying
ember. Opposite this warmth stands a silent arena, its entrance yawning
open beneath a fixed 'Closed' sign. Thick plumes of steam rise from the
northern rocks, veiling the path where the silver road finally dissolves
into stone and dust.

The pale stones of Silver Street terminate at the jagged base of a
mountainous peak. Thick, rhythmic plumes of soot and dull flame rise
from the summit, casting a heavy shroud over the valley. Along the high
ridges, dark silhouettes of orcish sentinels remain motionless against
the gray sky, their gaze fixed eternally upon the vacant streets below.
A silent storefront stands to the east, while a stone facade blocks the
view to the west.

A heavy chill hangs in the air of this cavernous smeltery, where the
great furnaces once roared. To the west, the street's gray light spills
across a layer of fine ash covering the service counter. A small, soot-
stained sign remains fixed to the stone wall, its lettering faded into
obscurity. To the east, a doorway leads into the shadows of a silent
backroom, stripped of the rhythmic hammers that once defined this space.

Iron tools lie scattered across heavy stone workbenches, coated in a
thick, undisturbed layer of grit. A large wooden sign hangs crookedly
from the wall, its painted instructions peeling away like dead skin.
The cheerful whistling that once filled the air has been replaced by
a hollow, oppressive silence. To the west, the dim archway leads back
into the cold expanse of the main smeltery.
